title: Granulated sugar for caster sugar in a dry mix

evidence.basis: B6. OD-7 (owner commission 2026-10-08, ENGINEERING only; not culinary validation, not released guidance). Evidence: private/research/substitution-knowledge (2026-10-07). Amount: KA SRC-SU-01#f ('Granulated sugar can be used in place of superfine sugar/caster sugar by weight'). Identity: KA SRC-SU-01#c (caster is granulated ground finer); UK law SRC-SU-27#a defines white sugar by purity, not grain size. Scope enforced: the sugar's only use (listed-total base), a dry mix that is then mixed into a dough (MIX_DOUGH) and baked, amount in grams. Grain-size consequence: Nigella.com SRC-SU-15#b/#c (UK granulated coarser), SRC-SU-16#a (undissolved crystals in creamed cakes; analogy). No source tests scones or biscuits.

consequence.headline: Use the same weight of granulated sugar instead of the caster sugar.
consequence.reason: Caster sugar is granulated sugar ground finer, so the same weight sweetens the same.
consequence.tradeoff: Granulated crystals are coarser and may not all dissolve, so the texture can be slightly grainier or speckled; UK granulated sugar is coarser still.

proposal.text: Yes, the same weight of granulated sugar.
